territorial_scope.description: Applies to AI operators (providers, deployers, users, importers and distributors) under the law; the text names importers of systems from abroad but states no explicit reach beyond national jurisdiction.

evidence.quote: This Law applies to providers, deployers, users, importers, and distributors of artificial intelligence systems, as well as to persons affected by such systems.

agora_harms: Violation of civil or human rights, including privacy

summary.short: Turkish bill on artificial intelligence. It sets principles (safety, transparency, fairness, accountability, privacy) for AI operators, requires risk assessment, registration and conformity assessment for high-risk systems, and provides administrative fines of up to 35 million TL or 7% of turnover for prohibited applications.
summary.long: The bill's purpose is to ensure safe, ethical and fair use of AI systems, to protect personal data and privacy, and to establish a regulatory framework for developing and using AI systems. It applies to providers, deployers, users, importers and distributors of AI systems and to persons affected by them. Article 3 lists five principles: safety, transparency, fairness, accountability and privacy. Article 4 requires risk assessments during development and use, special measures for high-risk systems, registration of high-risk systems with the relevant supervisory authorities, and a conformity assessment. Article 5 obliges operators to comply with the law and related regulations and gives supervisory authorities monitoring and detection powers. Article 6 sets fines of up to 35 million Turkish Liras or 7% of annual turnover for prohibited AI applications, up to 15 million Turkish Liras or 3% for breaches of obligations, and up to 7.5 million Turkish Liras or 1.5% for providing false information. The text refers to prohibited applications but does not set them out. The law enters into force on publication (Article 7) and is executed by the President (Article 8). The document is an introduced proposal and has not been enacted.

notes: Bill text as provided, at the introduced stage; the registry lists status pending. The text cites no other instrument by name or number and refers only generically to 'related regulations' (Art. 5) and 'personal data protection' (Art. 1), so no relations are coded. Article 6 amounts carry footnote markers (Liras1, Liras2, Liras3) that are not part of the amounts. Article 4 refers to 'relevant supervisory authorities' without naming them.

events.date_text: This Law shall enter into force on the date of its publication.

evidence.quote: This Law shall enter into force on the date of its publication.

relations.note: No references to other instruments by name or number; only generic references to 'related regulations' (Art. 5) and personal data protection (Art. 1).

thresholds.note: The text has no numeric cutoffs that change scope, eligibility, exemption, obligation tier or prohibition. The only figures are fine maxima in Article 6 (35 million, 15 million and 7.5 million Turkish Liras; 7%, 3% and 1.5% of annual turnover), which are coded as enforcement rather than thresholds. High-risk systems (Article 4) are not defined by a numeric cutoff in this text.
